goal_understood: Guard scope='complete' with a measured corpus cross-check (size, optional hash) so an operator string alone can never convert an unbundled real cite into a false 'no such case'; mismatches and unmeasured corpora fold to bounded could-not-check.

correctness.note: All four branches verified: (1) matching size+hash earns the loud miss (bounded=False, unsupported verdict, 'not found'+'complete as of' in reason); (2) oversized manifest folds to could-not-check (bounded=True, corpus_scope suppressed, 'unknown' verdict, no 'not found'/'no such case'); (3) size-match+wrong-hash folds to could-not-check; (4) client with attr deleted folds to could-not-check. Demo path (scope='demo') is entirely unchanged: bounded=True, emit_manifest_fields=True, corpus fields still emitted. The complete_honored gate in _annotate_litigator_verdicts is a short-circuit requiring manifest != None AND scope=='complete' AND attestation != None AND manifest.matches(attestation) — each condition individually guards the right failure mode. corpus_fingerprint is order-independent (sorted lines before sha256). No silent fallback; failures degrade to could-not-check, never to false green. 356 tests green, zero regressions.

test_coverage.note: 11 new tests across two test classes. CorpusAttestationCrossCheckTests pins both directions: matching earns the catch (test_matching_size_and_hash_complete_manifest_earns_the_catch), oversized folds (test_oversized_complete_manifest_folds_to_could_not_check), right-size wrong-hash folds (test_size_match_but_wrong_hash_folds_to_could_not_check), no-attr folds (test_complete_manifest_without_measurement_folds). CorpusFingerprintTests pins purity, order-independence, identity-sensitivity (add/rename/remove), size-only match, hash-override reject, and attest_corpus. Pre-existing CorpusManifestTests (4 tests) are a regression guard for the demo path and the complete path — they still pass. No skip/xfail added. 75 tests total in test_deterministic_envelope, 356 across the full suite.

security.note: Machine-verifiable: no network call introduced (zero-egress 7/7 green), no secrets in logs, no new external dependency (hashlib is stdlib), no new attack surface in terms of data exfiltration. The gate moves exclusively in the safe direction (could-not-check, never a widened false green). However: both local_caselaw.py and deterministic_envelope.py are on the contract's human_gates.security path ('verify-engine truth surfaces and the corpus-attestation path need a human read'). The security dimension cannot be FULL marks here — the unknown-unknown edge (e.g. a crafted corpus that collides the sha256 fingerprint, or a setattr side-channel on the httpx.Client) requires the human operator review the contract explicitly requests. Routing to human gate.

code_quality.note: New types (CorpusAttestation, corpus_fingerprint, attest_corpus) are tightly scoped frozen dataclasses with clear doc-strings. CORPUS_ATTESTATION_ATTR is a named constant, not a magic string. matches() carries a note explaining the asymmetry between size-only and hash-declared manifests. complete_honored + emit_manifest_fields decomposition in _annotate_litigator_verdicts is explicit and readable — each flag does exactly one thing. No dead code, no commented-out blocks. Ruff clean. Follows existing patterns (frozen dataclasses, module-level constants, inline E-tag comments). content_hash: str | None = None as a dataclass field with default is the right shape for optional gradual deployment.

alignment.note: All four E2 acceptance bullets satisfied: (1) scope='complete' honored only on size+hash match; (2) demo manifest path unchanged — verified by test_demo_manifest_rides_the_default_path and manual inspection; (3) both directions pinned in tests; (4) zero-egress holds, fingerprint is computed over in-memory dict only (no I/O).
